intent_en: To illustrate that while U.S. students score above the OECD average on PISA exams, they are outperformed by students in countries like Finland and Japan, which achieve higher scores with significantly fewer teaching hours.
previous_intent: To demonstrate the relative PISA scores of the U.S. compared to the OECD average and top performers like Finland and Singapore, while highlighting the counter-intuitive finding that higher-scoring countries have lower teaching hours.
narration_support: Students in the U .S. score slightly above the OECD average on the PISA exam... but they score lower than students in countries like Finland, South Korea, Japan, and Singapore, where teaching hours are much lower.
chart_support: Bar chart displaying PISA Scores (OECD, 2018) showing that Singapore (SGP), Japan (JPN), South Korea (KOR), and Finland (FIN) have higher scores than the USA (USA), with a dotted line indicating a threshold (likely the average).
evidence_note: The narration explicitly states the comparison between US scores and higher-scoring countries (Finland, Japan, etc.) and introduces the counter-intuitive factor of teaching hours. The chart visually confirms the score hierarchy where SGP, JPN, KOR, and FIN are all higher than USA.
